props.title: Four moments, four sizes of the same band.
props.lede: One or two musicians at the ceremony, two on the terrace, three at dinner and four on the floor, and the guests hear it as one band getting bigger.

rows.text: A solo jazz guitarist or the duo, playing a prelude of ballads while the seats fill, the processional you chose, and something with a lift in it for the walk back up the aisle.
Upright bass and guitar, at a level guests who’ve just met can talk across. Standards are the repertoire because nobody has to be told what they are.

The trio, with the drums played with brushes so the kit sits under the tables. The music stops for each toast while your speaker is still steps from the microphone. Changes Jazz Trio plays this size with a modern edge on the standards.

rows.term: The first dance and the floor
rows.text: The quartet, the trio plus a horn or a voice, playing the swing and the soul end of the standards book for the hour after the first dance, and the DJ carries the late end through the same sound system, on the same contract.

props.title: Asked about jazz bands for weddings.

items.q: Which size of jazz band does a wedding reception need?
items.a: It depends on what the floor is doing. Dinner wants the trio, drums played with brushes. A first dance and an open floor want the quartet, the trio plus a horn or a voice, and a ballroom of two hundred wants the quartet with a singer out front. Tell us the guest count and the venue and we'll recommend the size. Signet Artists books wedding jazz bands across Denver and the Colorado mountains.

At the ceremony and through the cocktail hour, gentle enough that guests greet each other over it; at dinner, the level of the conversation at the table; on the floor, the quartet plays like a dance band, up to what the venue allows.

items.q: Will a jazz band play our first dance?
items.a: Yes. If the song is a standard, it's probably already in the repertoire, and if it isn't, send the title with the date and we can usually learn it.

items.q: Is a jazz band the right choice for a wedding that wants dancing?
items.a: For a floor that wants to dance to songs it knows, a jazz quartet plays the swing and the soul side of the standards book and hands off to the DJ for the late end. For a floor that wants pop and rock all night, book a covers band for the reception and keep the jazz for the ceremony, the cocktail hour and dinner, on the same contract.
